A quick reminder about Rule 8 from the server rules: there can be times when we will step in to riff and improv on the things that catch our attention. There will be plenty of time to do what we call “Invitationals.” Invitationals are enacted when a player or a DM wants to follow through on an improv story line. They can be requested by anyone, but are fulfilled only as time and DM interest allows.

Please remember that while for players this can feel like a big open sandbox game, the things in it that you are interacting with are people who donate their time. Its a big job that is as taxing as it is rewarding. Talk to you DMs about what you would like to accomplish in down time and invitationals. And when it works for them to help generate the hours and hours of content we provide (for free and on top of your jobs, lives and everything else.) We love you. Most of the DMs have not endured this gauntlet before. Trust me, trying to put this event on is one of the most challenging things a dm will ever do.  Be patient courteous and kind to all of our volunteers. 
If a dm is running combat in voice, they might ask to keep mics closed when running. A very good habit to be in, is to pre type your action before your turn. Combat is long. You might have 20-30 minutes between rounds. Please do your best not to take extra time on your turn. It is a matter of kindness to your dms and courtesy to you fellow players. Remember to thank your mods, and listen to them when they mod combat and loot drops. Thanks

My memories begin six months ago. I awoke naked, a strange steam rising from my body and the smell of ozone in the air. On the floor of a ship, in the belly of the hold. In my arms I was clutching my battered and ancient brass horn. I was alone and cold, so so cold, and weak. I laid there for a time, trembling. My mind raced with all manner of strange thoughts; alchemical formulas, historical notations, scientific theorum.
After a time I rose. Near to me was a large crate. "T H E  D A V I D S O N  C O A T  C O M P A N Y" was stenciled boldly on it's side. "London/Pula/Shanghai/Sigil" and underneath: "STYLE: WINTERGREEN." Two of the wooden slats of the crate's lid were warped, allowing me to reach a hand through and draw out a huge green coat. As I did I saw my wrists were wet and raw with the wounds of imprisonment. I could not remember my name, or my past, only the jumbled and copius arcane encyclopedia that seemed to continue to blossom in my wracked brain.
I shrugged into the great coat for the first time and stumbled onto the deck of a ship. A crowd of immigrants was gathered there, in awe of their first view of Empire City. I joined them. "I hear you can be anything you want there." Someone near to me said. "I hear it is a land of opportunity." Someone else was telling thier brother, thier children, thier cousins and friends. The voices of the hopeful washed over me, a melange of languages and tones and musical accents. I simply become one of them. Who I was before, the naked man with the horn who wore the shackles, it didn't matter who he was. I didn't want to be him anymore anyway. So when someone on the ship asked me my name, I thought about the words stitched small on the inside of my new coat. "Call me Davidson Wintergreen" I told them. Then I got on the first unguarded skiff I lucked into and floated away, letting the breeze carry me where it might.

It carried me into a storm. Fierce winds of war, tidal waves of fear, bombs striking like lightning.

And now that storm has blown me away, dissipated my new identity, left me drifting and empty once again. I strain with all my might to once again recover some semblance of what was lost, to build a new man from the broken pieces left of the old. I gather everything I can of my awareness and will, focus, and begin to make myself once more.
